body.statement: The function \(r\mapsto H(r;f)\) is convex on the positive orthant. The exact-count problem over \(\Delta_K(\rho)\) and the nominal-label problem \(\min_{p\in\Delta_K}H(Bp;f)\) both attain their minima. A feasible \(rStar\) or \(pStar\) is globally optimal if and only if there exist at most \(K+1\) active pair-and-vertex scenarios \((i,j,\lambda)\), nonnegative weights summing to one, and a simplex normal such that the corresponding weighted gradients satisfy the KKT stationarity equation; primal activity, an LP dual certificate for each active \(\lambda\), and stationarity form a finite optimality certificate.
body.justification: The theorem turns covariance ambiguity into a certified choice of randomization rather than a post hoc sensitivity plot.
body.gap: BairdEtAl2018 optimizes power under maintained outcome structure, while JiangImaiMalani2023 fixes the assignment-mechanism distribution and uses conservative covariance analysis; neither gives a sharp-set minimax allocation with necessary-and-sufficient optimality witnesses.
body.consumer: The Kenya saturation design in EggerEtAl2022 can be re-planned on the \(m=(1,2,4)\) menu with a finite certificate showing which allocation minimizes worst-case pairwise policy uncertainty.
